classifications.notes: DQAG is the general adaptive finite-interval callback integrator; KEY selects its Gauss-Kronrod rule. The public declarations expose workspace/control arguments rather than automatic allocation. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: General finite-interval adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration. KEY chooses a 15/21/31/41/51/61-point rule pair (out-of-range values are clamped to the endpoint choices). Require LIMIT>=1, IWORK(LIMIT), LENW>=4*LIMIT and WORK(LENW). Supply absolute/relative tolerances; invalid tolerance combinations give IER=6. The integrand callback supplies the full ordinary integrand. The public quadpack module reexports these REAL64 DQ routines from quadpack_double, which preprocesses quadpack_generic.F90. F(X) is a scalar REAL64 function with REAL64 INTENT(IN) X. RESULT is the integral estimate, ABSERR an estimated absolute error, NEVAL a call count and LAST the partition count. IER=0 is normal algorithmic termination; nonzero values need routine-specific interpretation (invalid controls, exhausted subdivision or numerical difficulty), not unconditional acceptance. Error estimates are not certified bounds. Match default INTEGER and REAL64 types and provide finite callback values on the sampling domain.

This high-level wrapper initializes moment storage, rather than exposing the reusable-state ICALL/MOMCOM API. classifications.notes: The 1D object performs adaptive finite-interval Legendre-Gauss callback integration with explicit initialization and status/error outputs. procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(integration_class_1d) :: solver from quadrature_module. Configure the 1D scalar callback FX(ME,X), finite limits XL/XU, pseudorelative tolerance TOLX and integer METHODX. METHODX must be 6,8,10,12 or 14 (the quadrature point count); an invalid method causes ERROR STOP. It is an integer code, not a QUADRATURE_METHOD object. Callback ME is CLASS(INTEGRATION_CLASS_1D); match QUADRATURE_WP (REAL64 default). All controls shown are required. The callback pointer must remain valid for subsequent INTEGRATE calls. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(integration_class_1d) :: solver from quadrature_module. Integrate after successful initialization, returning scalar ANS, integer IERR and scalar ERR, all required outputs. IERR=1 is normal (including zero-width intervals), -1 flags nearly coincident limits, and 2 indicates likely insufficient accuracy. ERR is an estimated absolute error, not a certified bound or correction to add to ANS. The requested tolerance is pseudorelative to an integral of the absolute integrand; it is not a simple relative-error guarantee for a strongly cancelling integral. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

classifications.notes: LMDIF1 minimizes a sum of squared nonlinear residuals using values supplied by the caller and a finite-difference Jacobian. This derivative-free-user interface is a specialized least-squares optimizer, not a general arbitrary scalar-objective algorithm. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: Simplified Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least squares with M residuals, N variables and a forward-difference residual Jacobian. Require M>=N>0, TOL>=0, FVEC(M), IWA(N) and real WA(LWA) with LWA>=M*N+5*N+M. X(N) is input/output. FCN(M,N,X,FVEC,IFLAG) returns residual values for finite-difference calls, and may abort by setting IFLAG<0. INFO=0 signals invalid controls, negative values callback cancellation, 1..4 the documented reduction/step/orthogonality conditions, 5 evaluation exhaustion, 6..7 too-small tolerance; these are not a certificate of a zero residual or global minimum. The simplified wrapper fixes the budget to 200*(N+1), with no public counter output. All real arrays use REAL64 in this pinned module.

classifications.notes: LMDER1 minimizes the squared norm of caller residuals using an analytic residual Jacobian. That Jacobian provides first-derivative information for this particular scalar sum-of-squares objective; it is not a callback returning an arbitrary scalar objective gradient. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: Simplified nonlinear least squares with an analytic residual Jacobian. Require M>=N>0, LDFJAC>=M, FVEC(M), FJAC(LDFJAC,N), IPVT(N), WA(LWA) and LWA>=5*N+M. FCN(M,N,X,FVEC,FJAC,LDFJAC,IFLAG) fills residuals for IFLAG=1 and Jacobian for IFLAG=2 without altering the other buffer; negative IFLAG cancels. X is input/output. classifications.notes: The public FMIN function performs smooth scalar minimization without user derivatives over an initial interval. It uses safeguarded parabolic interpolation with golden-section fallback and a stopping scale SQRT(EPSILON)*ABS(X)+TOL/3. This modern package places F before AX/BX, unlike some textbook interfaces of the same name. The return is only a minimizer estimate; no convergence/status output or evaluation budget is exposed. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: Scalar derivative-free minimizer combining golden-section and parabolic steps. The objective function F(X) is the first argument, followed by ordered interval endpoints AX/BX and nonnegative TOL; the result XMIN is an abscissa, not the minimum function value. Reevaluate F(XMIN) if its value is needed. Import fmin_rk to match the preprocessed real kind (REAL64 by default); callback argument and result have that kind. The source has no status, iteration-count or maximum-evaluation argument; its unbounded loop exits on an interval/machine-precision condition. Finite objective values and a suitable unimodal interval are caller responsibilities; multimodal, invalid-input and nontermination behavior are not certified by this review. The upstream source filename is case-sensitive fmin_module.F90.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(slsqp_solver) :: solver from slsqp_module. Configure N variables, M total constraints, MEQ equality constraints, iteration/accuracy controls, objective/constraint callback F and gradient callback G. Callback F(ME,X,F,C) returns objective and constraints with equalities first; remaining inequalities use C>=0. G(ME,X,G,A) returns objective gradient G(N) and constraint Jacobian A(M,N), with CLASS(SLSQP_SOLVER) ME. XL/XU are real bound arrays of length N; match SLSQP_KINDS::SLSQP_RK (REAL64 default). Inspect required logical STATUS_OK. G is a required actual callback even when selecting finite-difference GRADIENT_MODE; modes 1..3 use absolute perturbations that do not respect bounds. Other optional controls/report callbacks are documented in linked declarations. Retain callbacks for optimization. The passed object ME in the linked implementation is supplied implicitly by solver%; do not pass it again.

classifications.notes: The public SETULB wrapper partitions workspace and calls MAINLB for smooth bound-constrained limited-memory BFGS using user objective gradients through reverse communication. The mapping requires real finite objective/gradient values and consistent bounds. It is not a derivative-free or callback-taking entry point. The character task state, workspace lengths, optional output-file argument and preprocessed kind selection are specific to this pinned modernized interface. This independent review records the public interfaces, dispatch and caller contracts, not a new numerical execution check or audit of every dependency/kernel. The existing problem-specific hosted drivers remain separate. No upstream numerical source is bundled.

procedures.summary: Reverse-communication bound-constrained minimization. Set TASK=START, preserve WA(2*M*N+5*N+11*M*M+8*M), IWA(3*N), CSAVE(60 characters), LSAVE(4), ISAVE(44), DSAVE(29), and all state across calls. When TASK begins FG, compute scalar F and gradient G(N) at returned X; NEW_X permits monitoring/continuation. CONV denotes a termination test, ABNO abnormal termination and ERROR invalid input; inspect the full TASK message and independently check the result. NBD values 0/1/2/3 mean unbounded/lower-only/both/upper-only; X/L/U/G are real arrays of length N, M is correction-history size. FACTR scales a relative objective-reduction tolerance by machine epsilon; PGTOL controls projected-gradient stopping. IPRINT<0 suppresses printing. The last ITERATION_FILE string is optional. No objective callback is passed to SETULB. Import lbfgsb_kinds_module::lbfgsb_wp to match the preprocessed library real kind (REAL64 by default); do not assume another fork has this optional argument or the same task representation.

procedures.summary: Return the right-handed cross product of REAL(WP) R(3) and V(3). Import WP from KIND_MODULE, whose default is REAL64 but which has build-time precision alternatives. Both vectors must use the same coordinate frame and consistent units; no physical units or frame conversion is inferred. This is a pure fixed-three-vector function with no status result, not an arbitrary-rank MATMUL replacement.

Normalize a rank-one REAL(WP) vector using NORM2. The result has SIZE(R); a zero norm produces a zero vector rather than a status or an arbitrary unit direction. Callers needing a nonzero direction must reject zero inputs themselves. No allocation/status actual is exposed and this scoped interface does not establish behavior for nonfinite vector data.

Rotate V(3) about axis K(3) through radian THETA using the right-handed Rodrigues formula, returning VROT(3), all REAL(WP). The routine normalizes K internally, so its magnitude is irrelevant for a nonzero axis. Require K nonzero: UNIT returns zeros for a zero axis and the resulting expression is not a valid general rotation. There is no status flag or automatic degrees conversion.

compute the function f.  it is to have the form
subroutine f (neq, t, y, ydot)
real(wp) t, y(neq), ydot(neq)
where neq, t, and y are input, and the array ydot = f(t,y)
is output.  y and ydot are arrays of length neq.

the name of the user-supplied routine (miter = 1 or 4) to
compute the jacobian matrix, df/dy, as a function of
the scalar t and the vector y.  it is to have the form [[f_jac]],
where neq, t, y, ml, mu, and nrowpd are input and the array
pd is to be loaded with partial derivatives (elements of the
jacobian matrix) in the output.  pd must be given a first
dimension of nrowpd.  t and y have the same meaning as in
subroutine f.
* in the full matrix case (miter = 1), ml and mu are
ignored, and the jacobian is to be loaded into pd in
columnwise manner, with df(i)/dy(j) loaded into pd(i,j).
* in the band matrix case (miter = 4), the elements
within the band are to be loaded into pd in columnwise
manner, with diagonal lines of df/dy loaded into the rows
of pd. thus df(i)/dy(j) is to be loaded into pd(i-j+mu+1,j).
ml and mu are the half-bandwidth parameters. (see iwork).
the locations in pd in the two triangular areas which
correspond to nonexistent matrix elements can be ignored
or loaded arbitrarily, as they are overwritten by dvode.
jac need not provide df/dy exactly.  a crude
approximation (possibly with a smaller bandwidth) will do.
in either case, pd is preset to zero by the solver,
so that only the nonzero elements need be loaded by jac.
each call to jac is preceded by a call to f with the same
arguments neq, t, and y.  thus to gain some efficiency,
intermediate quantities shared by both calculations may be
saved in a user common block by f and not recomputed by jac,
if desired.  also, jac may alter the y array, if desired.
jac must be declared external in the calling program.
the following subroutine is called just before each internal
integration step, and sets the array of error weights, ewt, as
described under itol/rtol/atol above:
`subroutine dewset (neq, itol, rtol, atol, ycur, ewt)`
where neq, itol, rtol, and atol are as in the [[dvode]] call sequence,
ycur contains the current dependent variable vector, and
ewt is the array of weights set by dewset.
if the user supplies this subroutine, it must return in ewt(i)
(i = 1,...,neq) a positive quantity suitable for comparison with
errors in y(i).  the ewt array returned by dewset is passed to the
dvnorm routine (see below.), and also used by dvode in the computation
of the optional output imxer, the diagonal jacobian approximation,
and the increments for difference quotient jacobians.
in the user-supplied version of dewset, it may be desirable to use
the current values of derivatives of y.  derivatives up to order nq

given by nst = 0, nq is 1 and h is temporarily set to 1.0.
nyh is the initial value of neq.  the quantities nq, h, and nst
can be obtained by including in dewset the statements:
```fortran
type(dvode_data_t) :: sav
call me%dvsrco(sav,job=1)
nq = sav%nq
h = sav%h
nst = sav%nst
thus, for example, the current value of dy/dt can be obtained as
`ycur(nyh+i)/h  (i=1,...,neq)`  (and the division by h is
unnecessary when nst = 0).
the following is a real function routine which computes the weighted
root-mean-square norm of a vector v:
`d = dvnorm (n, v, w)`
where:
* n = the length of the vector,
* v = real array of length n containing the vector,
* w = real array of length n containing weights,
dvnorm is called with n = neq and with w(i) = 1.0/ewt(i), where
ewt is as set by subroutine dewset.
if the user supplies this function, it should return a non-negative
value of dvnorm suitable for use in the error control in dvode.
none of the arguments should be altered by dvnorm.
for example, a user-supplied dvnorm routine might:
* substitute a max-norm of (v(i)*w(i)) for the rms-norm, or
* ignore some components of v in the norm, with the effect of
suppressing the error control on those components of y.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(dvode_t) :: solver from dvode_module. Integrate after INITIALIZE, retaining this object and caller-owned RWORK/IWORK between continuation calls. Y(NEQ) and scalar T are INOUT; RTOL/ATOL are arrays, even for scalar tolerances, selected by ITOL=1..4. Set ISTATE=1 for a new problem, ITASK=1 to return at TOUT, IOPT=0 for default controls. ISTATE=2 is successful return; negative values require diagnostic handling, and T may be short of TOUT. For nonstiff Adams MF=10 use LRW>=20+16*NEQ and LIW>=30; stiff BDF with internal dense Jacobian MF=22 requires LRW>=22+9*NEQ+2*NEQ**2 and LIW>=30+NEQ. Other MF/workspace/band controls follow the linked declarations. Match DVODE_WP, use nonnegative tolerances giving positive error weights, and do not reset continuation workspace. The passed object ME is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

2     scalar     array      rtol*abs(y(i)) + atol(i)

an index specifying the task to be performed.
input only.  itask has the following values and meanings:
* 1  means normal computation of output values of y(t) at

* 2  means take one step only and return.
* 3  means stop at the first internal mesh point at or
beyond t = tout and return.
* 4  means normal computation of output values of y(t) at

or beyond tout, but not behind it in the direction of
integration.  this option is useful if the problem
has a singularity at or beyond t = tcrit.
* 5  means take one step, without passing tcrit, and return.

indicate this (unless itask = 4 and tout comes before tcrit,

classifications.notes: The public bobyqa_module::bobyqa minimizes a smooth real scalar function under lower/upper variable bounds without supplied derivatives. It builds quadratic interpolation models and uses a trust-region method, dispatching to private BOBYQB. The selected public interface has ten arguments: N,NPT,X,XL,XU,RHOBEG,RHOEND,IPRINT,MAXFUN,CALFUN; it allocates workspace internally. This differs from older external BOBYQA interfaces with a user workspace and from other forks with status/F outputs. N must be at least 2; N+2<=NPT<=(N+1)*(N+2)/2; NPT=2*N+1 is a suggested initial choice. Provide conforming REAL(wp) vectors X/XL/XU of length at least N. wp is REAL64 in the pinned kind_module. Require positive RHOEND<=RHOBEG and each bound interval at least 2*RHOBEG wide; scale variables appropriately. The wrapper can adjust the initial X away from bounds to construct its interpolation model. CALFUN(N,X,F) is a subroutine callback with default INTEGER N, assumed-shape REAL(wp) X(:) INTENT(IN), and scalar REAL(wp) F INTENT(OUT). X is overwritten by the best estimate; neither objective value nor convergence status is an output argument. Reevaluate the callback to obtain F and independently assess the result. Invalid NPT or insufficient bound spacing prints a diagnostic and returns; normal return alone is not a success certificate. IPRINT=0 suppresses ordinary iteration output but not those wrapper diagnostics. MAXFUN limits callback evaluations; there is no public counter/status result. This review inspects the public wrapper, callback declarations and precision selection, not every private interpolation/trust-region kernel. The illustrative calling program was not compiled or run for this independent review. The existing playground box-quadratic checked driver remains separately recorded and is not reclassified as a new independent numerical test.

procedures.usage:
program bounded_minimum
  use kind_module, only: wp
  use bobyqa_module, only: bobyqa
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: n=2, npt=5
  real(wp) :: x(n), xl(n), xu(n), f
  x=[0.5_wp,0.5_wp]
  xl=[0.0_wp,0.0_wp]
  xu=[1.0_wp,1.0_wp]
  call bobyqa(n,npt,x,xl,xu,0.2_wp,1.0e-8_wp,0,1000,objective)
  call objective(n,x,f)
  print *, x, f
contains
  subroutine objective(n,x,f)
    integer, intent(in) :: n
    real(wp), intent(in) :: x(:)
    real(wp), intent(out) :: f
    f=(x(1)-2.0_wp)**2+(x(2)+1.0_wp)**2
  end subroutine objective
end program bounded_minimum
procedures.usage_notes: Illustrative complete calling program only; not compiled or run for this independent review. Provide the callback as an internal or module subroutine so its assumed-shape interface is explicit. The mathematical reference solution for this particular [0,1]^2 quadratic is X=(1,0), F=2, but no output from this illustration is claimed. This is not the separately checked playground driver. See the pinned declaration links for all inputs and callback types. Bounds, interpolation geometry, scale, evaluation budget and absence of a returned success flag remain caller responsibilities.

procedures.summary: Inverse transform from a rank-one COMPLEX(REAL64) half-spectrum. In this pin optional N counts complex bins to retain/pad, not the desired real output length. procedures.summary: Iterative real least squares with optional Tikhonov damping through mandatory DAMP (set zero for undamped). Aprod1(M,N,X,Y) must accumulate Y += A*X without altering X; Aprod2 must accumulate X += TRANSPOSE(A)*Y without altering Y. These callbacks add to, rather than replace, the output buffers. B(M) is input and X(N) output, not an initial guess. Match LSMR_WP and LSMR_IP from lsmrDataModule. ATOL/BTOL set matrix/RHS error tolerances; CONLIM controls the condition estimate, ITNLIM the budget, LOCALSIZE local reorthogonalization and NOUT<=0 suppresses logging. Inspect ISTOP and estimates NORMA/CONDA/NORMR/NORMAR/NORMX with ITN. The executable code uses 0 for zero solution, 1/2 residual/least-squares tests, 3 conditioning limit, 4/5 machine-precision tests, 6 machine conditioning and 7 iteration limit: some older declaration comments have different codes, so the linked executable termination tests are authoritative.

procedures.summary: Declare TYPE(tpca) :: solver from forpca. One-call PCA interface: rows of MATRIX are observations, columns variables; use at least two rows, at least two columns and 1<=NPC<=number of columns. Match KINDS::RK from the dependency. COEFF is a required allocatable output after optional NPC/METHOD, so use COEFF=... and METHOD=... keywords. Prefer METHOD="eig" for covariance eigenvalues: the default "svd" branch instead squares covariance singular values and divides by NCOL-1, which is not the usual PCA variance convention. SCORE is allocated with NCOL columns but only the first NPC are filled. EXPLAINED is percent normalized by the first NPC eigenvalues, not automatically total variance. MATRIX_APP uses inconsistent centering in this pin; omit it when relying on this interface. No status output is provided. Use a fresh TPCA object for each fit. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

Declare TYPE(tpca) :: solver from forpca. Release several internal arrays through the public FINALIZE binding. This is not a complete reusable-object reset in the pinned source: LATENT and EXPLAINED_VARIANCE remain allocated. Calling PCA again after this binding alone can therefore fail on allocation. A fresh scoped TPCA object for each independent fit avoids that reuse assumption; allocated components are released when the object leaves scope. The passed object THIS is implicit in solver%; do not pass it again. Optional actuals shown in brackets can be supplied by keyword.

procedures.summary: Open/create a database using a Fortran CHARACTER FILE_NAME, returning a default INTEGER status and TYPE(C_PTR) DB. This wrapper adds the C terminator; do not append one yourself. ":memory:" requests an in-memory database. Test the return against SQLITE_OK before queries. A failed open can still return an allocated handle that must be closed; no finalizer owns DB for you. Database files are confined to the current environment and sandbox lifetime.

Execute SQL using a valid DB handle. Required CALLBACK is TYPE(C_FUNPTR) and CLIENT_DATA TYPE(C_PTR); use C_NULL_FUNPTR/C_NULL_PTR for statements without row processing. With no callback SELECT rows are discarded, not printed automatically. An actual callback must be BIND(C) with the SQLite callback ABI and remain callable during execution. Optional ERRMSG is allocatable CHARACTER. Check the returned INTEGER against SQLITE_OK. In this pin the wrapper copies the native error string without freeing its allocation; prefer prepared-statement error handling for repeated failing queries.

Close a TYPE(C_PTR) DB via the package C wrapper, returning INTEGER(C_INT). Finalize prepared statements and release blob/backup objects first, then check SQLITE_OK. The C wrapper sets DB to null regardless of the native close return; on SQLITE_BUSY the connection may remain allocated even though this variable loses its handle. Do not assume null DB proves a successful close. This differs from passing the handle by VALUE to the raw SQLite C function.

GET_D1 scalar generic returns an allocatable REAL(Rkind) gradient vector indexed by the NVAR independent-variable order used during seeding. Construct/evaluate with NDERIV>=1 first. CCONTEXT is required: C_NULL_PTR selects default context. With explicit LENGTH no null terminator is needed. Check C_ASSOCIATED(code); on failure inspect ERRORCODE and zero-based ERROROFFSET. Allocate native match-result storage, returning TYPE(C_PTR). Match compiled CODE against an 8-bit SUBJECT using an allocated MATCH_DATA handle and required MCONTEXT (C_NULL_PTR for default). LENGTH/STARTOFFSET are PCRE2_SIZE byte/code-unit counts, with STARTOFFSET zero-based. (i.e. the algebraic sign of the step sizes) and the rough

input only.  ITASK has the following values and meanings.
* 1  means normal computation of output values of y(t) at
t = TOUT (by overshooting and interpolating).
* 2  means take one step only and return.
* 3  means stop at the first internal mesh point at or
beyond t = TOUT and return.
* 4  means normal computation of output values of y(t) at
t = TOUT but without overshooting t = TCRIT.
TCRIT must be input as RWORK(1).  TCRIT may be equal to
or beyond TOUT, but not behind it in the direction of
integration.  This option is useful if the problem
has a singularity at or beyond t = TCRIT.
* 5  means take one step, without passing TCRIT, and return.
TCRIT must be input as RWORK(1).
Note:  If ITASK = 4 or 5 and the solver reaches TCRIT
(within roundoff), it will return T = TCRIT (exactly) to
indicate this (unless ITASK = 4 and TOUT comes before TCRIT,
in which case answers at t = TOUT are returned first).
an index used for input and output to specify the
the state of the calculation.
On input, the values of ISTATE are as follows.
* 1  means this is the first call for the problem
(initializations will be done).  See note below.
* 2  means this is not the first call, and the calculation
is to continue normally, with no change in any input
parameters except possibly TOUT and ITASK.
(If ITOL, RTOL, and/or ATOL are changed between calls
with ISTATE = 2, the new values will be used but not
tested for legality.)
* 3  means this is not the first call, and the
calculation is to continue normally, but with
a change in input parameters other than
TOUT and ITASK.  Changes are allowed in
NEQ, ITOL, RTOL, ATOL, IOPT, LRW, LIW, JT, ML, MU,
and any optional inputs except H0, MXORDN, and MXORDS.
(See IWORK description for ML and MU.)
In addition, immediately following a return with
ISTATE = 3 (root found), NG and G may be changed.
(But changing NG from 0 to .gt. 0 is not allowed.)
Note:  A preliminary call with TOUT = T is not counted
as a first call here, as no initialization or checking of
input is done.  (Such a call is sometimes useful for the
purpose of outputting the initial conditions.)
Thus the first call for which TOUT .ne. T requires
ISTATE = 1 on input.
On output, ISTATE has the following values and meanings.
* 1  means nothing was done; TOUT = t and ISTATE = 1 on input.
* 2  means the integration was performed successfully, and
no roots were found.
* 3  means the integration was successful, and one or more
roots were found before satisfying the stop condition
specified by ITASK.  See JROOT.
* -1  means an excessive amount of work (more than MXSTEP
steps) was done on this call, before completing the
requested task, but the integration was otherwise
successful as far as T.  (MXSTEP is an optional input
and is normally 500.)  To continue, the user may
simply reset ISTATE to a value .gt. 1 and call again
(the excess work step counter will be reset to 0).
In addition, the user may increase MXSTEP to avoid
this error return (see below on optional inputs).
* -2  means too much accuracy was requested for the precision
of the machine being used.  This was detected before
completing the requested task, but the integration
was successful as far as T.  To continue, the tolerance
parameters must be reset, and ISTATE must be set
to 3.  The optional output TOLSF may be used for this
purpose.  (Note: If this condition is detected before
taking any steps, then an illegal input return
(ISTATE = -3) occurs instead.)
* -3  means illegal input was detected, before taking any
integration steps.  See written message for details.
Note:  If the solver detects an infinite loop of calls
to the solver with illegal input, it will cause
the run to stop.
* -4  means there were repeated error test failures on
one attempted step, before completing the requested
task, but the integration was successful as far as T.
The problem may have a singularity, or the input
may be inappropriate.
* -5  means there were repeated convergence test failures on
one attempted step, before completing the requested
task, but the integration was successful as far as T.
This may be caused by an inaccurate Jacobian matrix,
if one is being used.
* -6  means EWT(i) became zero for some i during the
integration.  Pure relative error control (ATOL(i)=0.0)
was requested on a variable which has now vanished.
The integration was successful as far as T.
* -7  means the length of RWORK and/or IWORK was too small to
proceed, but the integration was successful as far as T.
This happens when DLSODAR chooses to switch methods
but LRW and/or LIW is too small for the new method.
* -8  means that the user terminated the integration by setting
`ierr` < 0 in the function `f`, the jacobian `jac`, or the
root function `g`.
Note:  Since the normal output value of ISTATE is 2,
it does not need to be reset for normal continuation.
Also, since a negative input value of ISTATE will be
regarded as illegal, a negative output value requires the
user to change it, and possibly other inputs, before
calling the solver again.

comments.text: THIS IS THE OPTION SWITCH, WHICH SHOULD BE SET TO
0 UNLESS ONE OR MORE OF THE EXTRA OPTIONS DESCRIBED BELOW
IS USED. THE USER HAS SEVERAL EXTRA OPTIONS WHICH ARE ACTIVATED BY SETTING
IOPTN TO A VALUE OTHER THAN 0; MORE THAN ONE AT A TIME CAN BE USED.
IN PARTICULAR:
* IF THE ONES DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0, THEN THE USER SHOULD GIVE FORMULAS
IN FNSET FOR COMPUTING THE PARTIAL DERIVATIVES WHEN INDFN=1 AS DESCRIBED
ABOVE.
* IF THE USER SETS THE ONES DIGIT OF IOPTN TO 1, THEN INDFN WILL ALWAYS
BE 0 WHEN FNSET IS CALLED, AND THE PROGRAM WILL AUTOMATICALLY
APPROXIMATE THE PARTIAL DERIVATIVES WHEN REQUIRED USING THE FOLLOWING
CENTERED DIFFERENCE FORMULA:
PARTIAL DERIVATIVE WITH RESPECT TO THE JTH VARIABLE (WHERE 1 <= J
<= NPARM) OF THE FUNCTION WHOSE VALUE IS COMPUTED IN CONFUN(IPT,1)
(WHERE 1 <= IPT <= NUMGR) IS APPROXIMATELY THE VALUE OF THIS
FUNCTION WHEN THE JTH COMPONENT OF PARAM IS INCREASED BY DELT, MINUS
THE VALUE OF THIS FUNCTION WHEN THE JTH COMPONENT OF PARAM IS
DECREASED BY DELT, ALL DIVIDED BY 2.0*DELT, WHERE DELT = SQRT(B**(-ITT)),
WHERE B IS THE BASE FOR FOR FLOATING POINT NUMBERS AND ITT IS THE NUMBER
OF BASE B DIGITS IN THE MANTISSA.
* IF THE TENS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0, THE PROGRAM WILL NOT GIVE UP
UNTIL EITHER AN ITERATION FAILS TO PRODUCE A REDUCTION ABS(ENCHG) OF
MORE THAN 100.0*B**(-ITT) IN THE PRINCIPAL ERROR NORM, OR ITLIM
ITERATIONS HAVE BEEN USED.
* IF THE TENS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 1, THE PROGRAM WILL ALSO GIVE UP IF
ABS(ENCHG) < ENCSM FOR LIMSM CONSECUTIVE STEPS IN THE MAIN PART OF
THE PROGRAM (I.E. AFTER TYPE -1 AND TYPE -2 FEASIBILITY HAVE BOTH BEEN
ACHIEVED).  THIS OPTION MAY BE USEFUL IN SAVING SOME TIME BY
FORESTALLING A LONG STRING OF ITERATIONS AT THE END OF A RUN WITH ONLY
A TINY IMPROVEMENT IN EACH ONE.  ENCSM AND LIMSM ARE TRANSMITTED TO
CONMAX IN WORK(1) AND IWORK(1) RESPECTIVELY.  WORK(1) AND IWORK(1) DO
NOT NEED TO BE ASSIGNED VALUES IF THE TENS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0.
* IF THE HUNDREDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0 OR 2, THEN THE INTERNAL PARAMETER
NSTEP WILL BE GIVEN THE DEFAULT VALUE 1.  NSTEP IS THE NUMBER OF
RUNGE-KUTTA STEPS USED IN EACH RK ITERATION.
* IF THE HUNDREDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 1 OR 3, THEN THE VALUE OF NSTEP USED
WILL BE THE POSITIVE INTEGER VALUE PLACED IN IWORK(2) BY THE USER IN THE
DRIVER PROGRAM.  SETTING NSTEP LARGER THAN 1 MAY ALLOW THE PROGRAM TO
SUCCEED ON DIFFICULT PROBLEMS WHERE THE CONVERGENCE WOULD BE EXTREMELY
SLOW WITH NSTEP=1, BUT IT WILL GENERALLY CAUSE MORE COMPUTER TIME TO BE
USED IN EACH RK ITERATION.  IWORK(2) DOES NOT NEED TO BE ASSIGNED A
VALUE IF THE HUNDREDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0 OR 2.  (NSTEP IS SOMETIMES
CALLED THE OVERDRIVE PARAMETER.)
* IF THE HUNDREDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0 OR 1, THEN THE INTERNAL PARAMETER
TOLCON WILL BE GIVEN THE DEFAULT VALUE SQRT(B**(-ITT)), WHERE B IS THE
BASE FOR FLOATING POINT NUMBERS AND ITT IS THE NUMBER OF BASE B DIGITS
IN THE MANTISSA.
* IF THE HUNDREDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 2 OR 3, THEN THE VALUE OF TOLCON USED
WILL BE THE VALUE PLACED IN WORK(2) BY THE USER IN THE DRIVER PROGRAM.
THIS VALUE SHOULD ALWAYS BE NONNEGATIVE.  IF THERE ARE NO TYPE -2 OR -1
CONSTRAINTS THEN THE SETTING OF TOLCON WILL HAVE NO EFFECT, BUT IF
THERE ARE TYPE -2 OR -1 CONSTRAINTS THEN IN GENERAL SMALLER VALUES OF
TOLCON MAY GIVE MORE ACCURACY IN THE FINAL ANSWER, BUT MAY SLOW DOWN
OR PREVENT CONVERGENCE, WHILE LARGER VALUES OF TOLCON MAY HAVE THE
REVERSE EFFECT.  IN PARTICULAR, IF THE TYPE -2 AND -1 CONSTRAINTS
CANNOT BE SATISFIED SUMULTANEOUSLY WITH STRICT INEQUALITY (THIS CASE
COULD OCCUR, FOR EXAMPLE, IF AN EQUALITY CONSTRAINT G = 0.0 WAS
ENTERED AS THE TWO INEQUALITY CONSTRAINTS G <= 0.0 AND
-G <= 0.0), THEN SETTING TOLCON=0.0 WILL ALMOST CERTAINLY CAUSE THE
PROGRAM TO FAIL, SINCE AT EACH ITERATION THE PROGRAM WILL NOT ACCEPT
PROSPECTIVE NEW VALUES OF THE PARAMETERS UNLESS IT CAN CORRECT THEM
BACK INTO THE RELAXED FEASIBLE REGION WHERE CONFUN(IPT,1) <= TOLCON
FOR ALL THE TYPE -2 AND -1 CONSTRAINTS.
* IF THE THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0, THE PROGRAM WILL USE THE RK METHOD
(WHICH INVOLVES APPLYING FOURTH ORDER RUNGE-KUTTA TO A SYSTEM OF
DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS), THEN IF THIS FAILS IT WILL TRY TO REDUCE
W WITH AN SLP STEP (I.E. SUCCESSIVE LINEAR PROGRAMMING WITH A TRUST
REGION), THEN GO BACK TO RK IF THE SLP STEP REDUCES W.
* IF THE THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 1, THE PROGRAM WILL USE SLP STEPS ONLY.
IN GENERAL, IN SOME PROBLEMS SLP WORKS VERY WELL, AND IN THOSE
PROBLEMS IT WILL USUALLY BE FASTER THAN RK BECAUSE IT REQUIRES FEWER
GRADIENT EVALUATIONS THAN RK, BUT IN OTHER PROBLEMS THE CONVERGENCE
OF SLP MAY BE EXCRUCIATINGLY SLOW, AND THE MORE POWERFUL RK METHOD
MAY BE MUCH FASTER.
* IF THE THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 2 THE PROGRAM WILL USE THE RK METHOD
ONLY, QUITTING WHEN RK CAN NO LONGER PRODUCE AN IMPROVEMENT.  THIS
MAY GIVE A LITTLE LESS ACCURACY THAN SETTING THE THOUSANDS DIGIT TO 0,
BUT MAY SAVE SIGNIFICANT COMPUTER TIME IN SOME CASES.
* IF THE TEN THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 0, THEN FNSET SHOULD BE WRITTEN AS
DESCRIBED ABOVE.
* IF THE USER SETS THE TEN THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN TO 1, THEN FNSET SHOULD BE
WRITTEN AS DESCRIBED ABOVE EXCEPT THAT THE COMPUTATIONS SHOULD BE DONE
FOR ALL IPT=1,..,NUMGR INSTEAD OF FOR A SINGLE GIVEN VALUE OF IPT.
THIS OPTION MAY SAVE COMPUTER TIME IN PROBLEMS WHERE A LARGE PART OF
THE COMPUTATION IS THE SAME FOR DIFFERENT VALUES OF IPT, SINCE IT
AVOIDS UNNECESSARY REPITITION OF THIS COMMON COMPUTATION BY HAVING
THE LOOP OVER IPT IN FNSET INSTEAD OF OUTSIDE FNSET.
IF THE TEN THOUSANDS DIGIT OF IOPTN IS 1, EVEN MORE TIME CAN OFTEN BE
SAVED IF FNSET IS WRITTEN SO THAT ALL CONSTRAINTS ARE COMPUTED IF IPT=0,
BUT ONLY THE STANDARD (I.E. TYPE -1 OR -2) CONSTRAINTS ARE COMPUTED IF

WILL BE POSITIVE WHENEVER FNSET IS CALLED, INDICATING THAT ONLY
CONSTRAINT IPT SHOULD BE COMPUTED.
THE DRAWBACK OF USING THIS OPTION IS THAT IN GENERAL SOME CONSTRAINT
VALUES AND DERIVATIVES WILL BE COMPUTED UNNECESSARILY, WHICH COULD COST
TIME IN SOME PROBLEMS.

UNLESS NO FUN(I) IS USED, IN WHICH CASE IT MUST BE >= 1.
(MATRIX ARRAY OF DIMENSION (IPTB,INDM))
ROW I OF THIS ARRAY NORMALLY CONTAINS A POINT USED IN THE ITH
CONSTRAINT.  THE ENTRIES IN ROW I NEED NOT BE ASSIGNED VALUES IF
SUCH A POINT IS NOT USED IN THE ITH CONSTRAINT.
(EXAMPLE:  IF THE LEFT SIDE OF CONSTRAINT I IS A POLYNOMIAL IN
ONE INDEPENDENT VARIABLE, THEN THE VALUE OF THE INDEPENDENT
VARIABLE SHOULD BE IN PTTBL(I,1), AND THE COEFFICIENTS SHOULD BE
IN PARAM.)
PTTBL CAN ALSO BE USED TO PASS OTHER INFORMATION FROM THE DRIVER
PROGRAM TO SUBROUTINE FNSET.
THIS IS THE FIRST DIMENSION OF PTTBL IN THE DRIVER
PROGRAM.  IT MUST BE >= THE LARGEST SUBSCRIPT I FOR WHICH A
VALUE PTTBL(I,J) IS USED, AND MUST BE >= 1 IF NO SUCH VALUES
ARE USED.
THIS IS THE SECOND DIMENSION OF PTTBL IN THE DRIVER
PROGRAM.  IT MUST BE >= THE LARGEST SUBSCRIPT J FOR WHICH A
VALUE PTTBL(I,J) IS USED, AND MUST BE >= 1 IF NO SUCH VALUES
ARE USED.
(VECTOR ARRAY OF DIMENSION LIWRK)  THIS IS AN INTEGER
WORK ARRAY.  THE USER NEED NOT PLACE ANY VALUES IN IT, EXCEPT
POSSIBLY CERTAIN OPTIONAL INFORMATION AS DESCRIBED BELOW.
THIS IS THE DIMENSION OF IWORK IN THE DRIVER PROGRAM.
IT MUST BE AT LEAST 7*NUMGR + 7*NPARM + 3.  IF NOT, CONMAX WILL
RETURN WITH THIS MINIMUM VALUE MULTIPLIED BY -1 AS A WARNING.
(VECTOR ARRAY OF DIMENSION LWRK)  THIS IS A FLOATING
POINT WORK ARRAY.  THE USER NEED NOT PLACE ANY VALUES IN IT,
EXCEPT POSSIBLY CERTAIN OPTIONAL INFORMATION AS DESCRIBED BELOW.
THIS IS THE DIMENSION OF WORK IN THE DRIVER PROGRAM.
IT MUST BE AT LEAST 2*NPARM**2 + 4*NUMGR*NPARM + 11*NUMGR +
27*NPARM + 13.  IF NOT, CONMAX WILL RETURN WITH THIS MINIMUM
VALUE MULTIPLIED BY -1 AS A WARNING.
THIS IS THE NUMBER OF ITERATIONS PERFORMED BY CONMAX,
INCLUDING THOSE USED IN ATTEMPTING TO GAIN FEASIBILITY,
UNTIL EITHER IT CAN NO LONGER IMPROVE THE SITUATION OR THE
ITERATION LIMIT IS REACHED.  IF ITER=ITLIM IT IS POSSIBLE
THAT THE PROGRAM COULD FURTHER REDUCE W IF RESTARTED
(POSSIBLY WITH THE NEW PARAMETERS).
* ITER=-1 IS A SIGNAL THAT TYPE -1 FEASIBILITY COULD NOT BE
ACHIEVED, IN THIS CASE ERROR WILL CONTAIN THE VALUES COMPUTED
USING THE USER SUPPLIED INITIAL APPROXIMATION.
* ITER=-2 IS A SIGNAL THAT TYPE -1 FEASIBILITY WAS ACHIEVED
BUT TYPE -2 FEASIBILITY COULD NOT BE ACHIEVED,
IN THIS CASE VALUES IN ERROR CORRESPONDING TO TYPE 1 OR
TYPE 2 CONSTRAINTS WILL BE ZERO.
(VECTOR ARRAY OF DIMENSION AT LEAST NPARM
IN THE DRIVER PROGRAM)  THE USER SHOULD PLACE AN INITIAL GUESS
FOR THE PARAMETERS IN PARAM, AND ON OUTPUT PARAM WILL CONTAIN
THE BEST PARAMETERS CONMAX HAS BEEN ABLE TO FIND.  IF THE
INITIAL PARAM IS NOT FEASIBLE THE PROGRAM WILL FIRST TRY TO
FIND A FEASIBLE PARAM.
(VECTOR ARRAY OF DIMENSION AT LEAST NUMGR + 3 IN THE
DRIVER PROGRAM)  FOR I=1,...,NUMGR, CONMAX WILL PLACE IN
ERROR(I) THE ERROR IN CONSTRAINT I (DEFINED TO BE THE VALUE
OF THE LEFT SIDE OF CONSTRAINT I, EXCEPT WITHOUT THE ABSOLUTE
VALUE IN TYPE 2 CONSTRAINTS).  FURTHER,
* ERROR(NUMGR+1) WILL BE THE (PRINCIPAL) ERROR NORM, THAT IS, THE
MAXIMUM VALUE OF THE LEFT SIDES OF THE TYPE 2 (INCLUDING THE
ABSOLUTE VALUE) AND TYPE 1 CONSTRAINTS.
* ERROR(NUMGR+2) WILL BE THE MAXIMUM VALUE OF THE LEFT SIDES OF THE
TYPE -1 CONSTRAINTS, OR 0.0 IF THERE ARE NO TYPE -1
CONSTRAINTS.  EXCEPT FOR ROUNDOFF ERROR AND SMALL TOLERANCES
IN SOME SUBROUTINES THIS VALUE WILL NORMALLY BE <= 0.0, AND
IT WILL NOT BE ALLOWED TO BE > TOLCON IN THE MAIN PART OF
THE PROGRAM.
* ERROR(NUMGR+3) WILL BE THE MAXIMUM VALUE OF THE LEFT SIDES OF THE
TYPE -2 CONSTRAINTS, OR 0.0 IF THERE ARE NO TYPE -2
CONSTRAINTS.  THIS VALUE SHOULD BE <= TOLCON, SINCE THE
PROGRAM WILL NOT EVEN ATTEMPT TO COMPUTE VALUES FOR THE
TYPE 2 AND TYPE 1 CONSTRAINTS OTHERWISE (EXCEPT FOR VALUES
CORRESPONDING TO THE INITIAL PARAMETERS PLACED IN PARAM BY
THE USER).  THE USER CAN USE THIS FEATURE TO INSERT TYPE -2
OR -1 CONSTRAINTS TO KEEP THE PARAMETERS AWAY FROM VALUES
WHERE A TYPE 2 OR TYPE 1 CONSTRAINT IS UNDEFINED.

procedures.summary: Allocate and initialize allocatable REAL(WP) WAVETABLE(:) for regular-grid scalar analysis at NLAT/NLON. Check ERROR_FLAG=0 before SHAEC. This is the allocating convenience wrapper around SHAECI, so the caller does not calculate a legacy wavetable length. An INTENT(OUT) allocatable actual is replaced on reinitialization. Reuse the resulting table only for the same grid and do not modify it. The synthesis table is initialized separately by INITIALIZE_SHSEC.

Analyze NT scalar fields on a regular latitude/longitude sphere into the package normalized real harmonic coefficients A/B. For the basic full-sphere case ISYM=0, use G(IDG,JDG,NT) with IDG>=NLAT, JDG>=NLON; theta(i)=(i-1)*pi/(NLAT-1) includes both poles, longitude has NLON distinct points without a repeated 2*pi endpoint. NLAT>=3, NLON>=4. A/B are (MDAB,NDAB,NT), NDAB>=NLAT and MDAB at least MIN(NLAT,(NLON+2)/2) for even NLON or MIN(NLAT,(NLON+1)/2) for odd NLON. Initialize WSHAEC first and check IERROR. ISYM=1/2 use different half-sphere storage. Do not substitute a Gaussian latitude grid.

Allocate and initialize a distinct REAL(WP) WAVETABLE(:) for regular-grid scalar SYNTHESIS. Check ERROR_FLAG before SHSEC, retain the table unchanged for repeated synthesis at the same NLAT/NLON, and reinitialize after grid-size changes. This initializes tables only, not harmonic coefficients or output fields. Do not assume an analysis table is interchangeable with this synthesis table.

Synthesize NT regular-grid scalar fields G from the package A/B harmonic coefficients. With ISYM=0 use the same full-sphere dimensions, grid order and coefficient normalization as SHAEC; NDAB>=NLAT and MDAB obeys the linked parity rule. G is an output array and A/B are input. Initialize WSHSEC for this grid with INITIALIZE_SHSEC and inspect IERROR before using G. Arbitrary samples need not survive an analysis/synthesis round trip exactly: unresolved harmonic content is projected away. Gaussian-grid synthesis uses a different entry point.

Solve a radial bound-state eigenproblem with REAL(DP) R/Rp/V on the same mesh and P/Q output arrays of matching extent. Supply n>0, 0<=l<n, energy guess EIN, positive EPS/MAX_ITER and a valid energy bracket EMIN_INIT/EMAX_INIT. Load/compile CHARACTER source onto the Lua stack; this convenience wrapper appends C_NULL_CHAR. Integer return zero means the chunk loaded, not that it has executed. Run the loaded chunk with LUA_PCALL; on loading failure inspect/clear the error object instead of calling it. The stack state is explicit and persists across operations.

Execute the function/chunk already on the Lua stack using required default-integer NARGS/NRESULTS/MSGH. For a freshly loaded zero-argument chunk requesting one returned value use 0,1,0, and check integer status zero before reading the result. Argument/result values are stack entries, not Fortran output dummies; MSGH=0 selects no custom message handler. A failed call leaves an error object. Remove results/errors deliberately before repeated calls and keep the interpreter live.

Convert stack index IDX to REAL(LUA_NUMBER) and check the separate numeric-conversion flag. Pass INTEGER(C_INT) IDX, for example -1_C_INT, and ISNUM=C_LOC(flag) where flag is INTEGER(C_INT),TARGET. ISNUM is a TYPE(C_PTR),VALUE native pointer, not a logical output actual. A numeric zero alone does not establish conversion success. This reads a live stack slot; it does not pop it.

Close one owning interpreter after every stack/borrowed-value use ends. The C_PTR actual is passed by VALUE, so this binding does not nullify the caller handle. Set that variable to C_NULL_PTR if retained and avoid double close through aliases. This is not automatic Fortran finalization or a stack-only reset.
